thesis: Realized operating expansion and profitability carry a conditional long-horizon growth case. Positive $21.4bn quarterly FCF supplies present cash support, while no valuation margin of safety or tactical bottom is established. The ruling supports bounded growth exposure rather than urgent aggressive entry.
strongest_counterexample: Quarterly FCF fell from $48.587bn to $21.4bn and the price has negative short-term momentum; strong revenue can coexist with worsening owner cash conversion at an unverified valuation.
invalidation_conditions: Two subsequent comparable quarters with year-over-year revenue growth at or below 0% would invalidate the sustained operating-growth foundation.
Two consecutive reported quarters with free cash flow at or below zero would invalidate reliance on durable current cash generation.
evidence_gaps: Complete refreshed liquidity and debt maturity assessment.
decisive_factors: Revenue and margins show strong realized operations.
Quarterly FCF is positive but below the previous quarter.
Oracle expansion plans are not recognized incremental revenue.
